spec.title: Dry-run: quorum reads and writes
spec.intro: About 6 minutes. The coordinator is twenty lines. Spend your time on why R + W > N works and what happens when replicas disagree.

steps.title: Write the rule down before any code
steps.explain: State the inequality and the pigeonhole argument behind it. If the read set and the write set together exceed the replica count they must overlap, so a read cannot miss the newest acknowledged write.
steps.saysOutLoud: R plus W greater than N means the read set and write set must share a replica.

steps.title: Any node can coordinate
steps.explain: There is no primary. Whichever node the client reaches coordinates that operation, which removes the single point of failure and all the failover machinery a primary would need. The replica set for a key comes from the hash ring.

steps.title: The quorum write
steps.explain: Send to all N, resolve as soon as W succeed. Latency is set by the second-fastest replica rather than the slowest, which is why a straggler does not slow the system — worth saying, because it is not obvious.
steps.saysOutLoud: I wait for W acks, not all N, so one slow replica doesn't slow the write.

steps.title: The quorum read, and picking a winner
steps.explain: Reading R replicas guarantees the newest value is among the responses — but you still have to identify it. Comparing versions is a separate step from reaching quorum, and conflating the two is a common slip.

steps.title: Repair the replicas you actually read
steps.explain: Read repair fixes the stale replicas that appeared in this read's responses — not the ones you skipped. That distinction matters, because it means read repair alone never fixes keys nobody reads.
steps.saysOutLoud: Read repair only touches replicas that answered. Cold keys need something else.

steps.title: Anti-entropy covers the keys nobody reads
steps.explain: Replicas periodically exchange Merkle trees of their key ranges and descend only where the hashes differ, so reconciling transfers a handful of hashes instead of the whole dataset. This is what actually delivers the 'eventually' in eventual consistency for cold data, and it runs continuously in the background rather than on the request path.

steps.title: Detect genuine conflicts instead of guessing
steps.explain: Two clients writing through different coordinators during a partition produce versions with no ordering between them. Vector clocks tell you they are concurrent rather than ordered — the value is the detection, because last-write-wins by timestamp silently discards one update.

steps.title: Turn the dial per operation
steps.explain: The strongest version of this answer ties the setting to the product rather than the database. Same store, two settings, each justified by what breaks when the data is stale.
steps.saysOutLoud: The cart reads at R=2 so users see their own writes; recommendations read at R=1.

spec.closing: If they ask about hinted handoff: a write for a node that is down is held by a peer with a hint and forwarded on recovery, so short outages don't drop writes or fail the quorum.
